correctness.rationale: A_n and C_n have dimensions 4n-3 and 4n-4. The type-A Weyl numerator for weight omega1+omega2 has 2^(2n-2) over positive-root denominators (2n-1)!(2n-2)!, yielding the displayed ordinary degree. Type-C complement to Levi C_(n-2) has 4n-4 positive roots and numerator 3*2^(2n-3) over (2n-1)!(2n-3)!, giving isotropic degree. Schubert-cell W/W_P gives 2n(2n-1) and 4n(n-1) Euler counts. Exact algebra gives the two ratios, and q_n-q_(n+1)=3/[(4n-3)(4n+1)]>0. Independently checked n=2..9 with exact rational arithmetic; source nested verifier checks n=2..100.
residual_risks: The result is specific to line–plane flags over C and O(1,1), not all isotropic flags or polarizations.

value.rationale: The natural codimension-one inclusion of symplectic isotropic flags into ordinary line–plane flags provides genuine geometric motivation for comparing degree and Euler characteristic under the same polarization. The exact competing suppression factors and their monotone sharp 3/4 normalized limit quantify distinct global invariants of this inclusion, rather than an arbitrarily selected polynomial value. The general computational tools themselves remain classical.
residual_risks: The answer is specialized and derivable using standard representation theory; its contribution is an exact natural comparison, not a new general Schubert theorem.

final_claim: For n>=2, ordinary A_n=F(1,2;2n) and isotropic C_n=SF(1,2;2n) under O(1,1), deg C_n/deg A_n=3(n-1)/(4n-3); chi(C_n)/chi(A_n)=2(n-1)/(2n-1), with normalized ratio 3(2n-1)/(2(4n-3)) decreasing from 9/10 to 3/4.
limitations: Only flag dimensions 1,2 in even-dimensional ambient vector space and Segre–Plücker polarization.
